text:
Alex M: quick idea — want to refactor the intake-adapter into a lightweight 'model descriptor' + pluggable 'probe adapters'. keeps static checks cheap and moves heavy benching behind opt-in probes.
Sara Chen: sounds promising. can you spell out the interface boundaries you have in mind?
Alex M: yeah. descriptor = small json blob with manifest, tokenizer hash, input shapes, quantization hints, and a canonical sample. static validators only read descriptor. probe adapters implement runtime checks (latency, kv-cache behavior, decode parity) and are separate processes.
Tom G: worried about migration complexity. how do we handle older models that only have adapters?
Alex M: fallback: if descriptor missing, we synthesize descriptor from existing adapter metadata (best-effort). new ingestion path prefers explicit descriptor and validates it with a 'descriptor-lint' step.
Kai L: example descriptor pls — small snippet is fine.
Alex M: ```json
{
  "model_id": "zeta-7b-v2",
  "tokenizer_sha256": "a1b2...",
  "max_seq": "2048",
  "quant": "int8-q4_0",
  "canonical_sample": "{\"prompt\": \"Hello world\"}",
  "acceptance_threshold": "0.88"
}
```
Sara Chen: acceptance_threshold OK, but we should avoid hard-coding numeric policies. maybe descriptor carries metadata and we store rules in policy engine.
Alex M: agree — descriptor has soft hints. policy engine maps hints -> required probe suites.
Tom G: probe adapters — do you mean a shared binary with plugins or independent containerized runners?
Alex M: independent runners (containers) to keep security boundaries. a light RPC (grpc) contract for probes: run_probe({descriptor, probe_name}) -> {score, logs, artifacts_url}.
Kai L: nice. how about cost? running many probes for every intake will blow budget.
Alex M: plan: tiered probing. quick probes (tokenizer, shape, smoke decode) run automatically. deep probes (latency p95 under load, quantization regression) are scheduled or gated behind commit thresholds/feature flags.
Sara Chen: also add a reproducibility tag on descriptor so we can re-run the exact probe suite later for audits.
Alex M: yes — descriptor includes provenance fields (uploader, commit, docker image tag) and a reproducible seed.
Tom G: rolling out: feature flag on ingestion, run in 'observe' mode for 2 weeks (no blocking). then escalate to blocking only if descriptor fails static lint.
onboard-bot: [deploy-bot] descriptor-lint job queued for zeta-7b-v2, run_id=2026-03-22-01
Sara Chen: what about tokenizers that change behavior across versions (non-deterministic)? tokenize parity probe should compare token sequences for canonical sample across reference tokenizer. if mismatch > N tokens -> fail.
Alex M: agreed. also add a 'semantic-sanity' probe using embeddings similarity on canonical_sample to catch subtle decode shifts. cheap and fast.
Kai L: interface question: where do probe artifacts live? we already have bench-artifacts S3. attach artifacts_url in probe response. keep retention policy conservative.
Alex M: use bench-artifacts with 30d hot retention + cold archive. artifacts_url included in registry entry.
Tom G: one more tradeoff: putting too much logic into descriptor encourages duplicating policy in consumers. keep descriptor minimal. policy engine does the heavy thinking.
Sara Chen: sounds like we're aligned. next steps?
Alex M: I'll draft an RFC that includes: descriptor schema, probe grpc contract, migration script for existing adapters, rollout plan + cost estimate. can I get reviewers from infra and platform? @Tom G @Kai L
Tom G: happy to review.
Kai L: same, will review for platform integration notes.
Sara Chen: I'll review probe definitions (smoke vs deep).
Alex M: thanks — I'll open the RFC today and link it here. :rocket:
